title: How Many Thoughts Can a Vector Hold? The Capacity of Reasoning by Superposition
abstract: arXiv:2609.13747v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models solve hard problems through intermediate computations across multi-step reasoning. Traditional chain-of-thought encodes these computations as tokens. Recent continuous and recurrent methods instead move partial computations into fixed-dimensional latent states, where a single thought can superpose multiple alternatives. This raises a fundamental design question:what should continuous thoughts preserve as reasoning proceeds? An intuitive approach discards past computations and keeps only the current reasoning frontier. Storing more items seems to dilute states and waste limited representational capacity. We show this intuition can be incorrect. Under identical downstream computations, cumulative superposition retaining full reasoning history can require lower representational dimensions than frontier-only superposition holding only current alternatives. translated_title: 一个向量能容纳多少想法？叠加推理的容量
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型通过多步推理中的中间计算来解决困难问题。传统的思维链方法将这些计算编码为token。而最近的连续推理和循环推理方法则将部分计算转移至固定维度的潜在状态中，其中单个思维可以叠加多个备选方案。这引出了一个基本的设计问题：随着推理的进行，连续思维应该保留什么？一种直观的做法是丢弃过去的计算，只保留当前的推理前沿。因为存储更多的项目似乎会稀释状态表示并浪费有限的表征容量。我们证明这种直觉可能是错误的。在相同的下游计算条件下，保留完整推理历史的累积叠加方式，可能比仅保留当前备选方案的前沿叠加方式需要更低的表征维度。在固定的隐藏层宽度下，这一优势使潜在推理器能够……
tldr: 该论文提出一个反直觉的发现：在潜在空间推理中，保留完整推理历史的“累积叠加”方式比只保留当前推理前沿的“前沿叠加”方式所需的表征维度更低，说明记住更多信息反而能更高效地利用有限的向量容量。
en_tdlr: Counterintuitively, this paper shows that cumulative superposition—retaining the full reasoning history in latent states—can require lower representational dimensions than frontier-only superposition, demonstrating that storing more information can make more efficient use of a vector's limited capacity for reasoning.
